stem: How does this reflection by Adams symbolize the motto E Pluribus Unum?

options.label: A
options.text: The many colonies were different yet came together to form one country.

options.label: B
options.text: As one country, the colonies divided into many to confuse the British.

options.label: C
options.text: Despite some differences between the colonies, the country was loyal to the British.

options.label: D
options.text: The divisions that existed between the colonies weakened the new country.

visual_elements:
The Colonies had . . . so great a Variety of Religions, they were composed of So many different Nations, their Customs, Manners and Habits had So little resemblance . . . that to unite them in the Same Principles in Theory and the Same System of Action was certainly a very difficult Enterprise. The complete Accomplishment of it, in So Short a time and by Such Simple means, was perhaps a Singular Example in the History of Mankind. Thirteen Clocks were made to Strike together; a perfection of Mechanism which no Artist had ever before effected.
—John Adams, letter to H. Niles, February 13, 1818
